args.title: Triage issue 4426
args.body:
File: src/util/money.ts

Architecture documentation and src/util/money.ts show that transaction amounts are parsed from the input file and stored as exact integer minor units (bigint) rather than floating-point numbers. Currencies with no minor unit (such as JPY, KRW, CLP, ISK, VND, XAF, XOF) are correctly handled by minorDigits() returning 0 decimal places, multiplying by 10^0 (1) to store them as whole units.

args.title: Triage issue 4429
args.body:
File: src/api/reports.ts

When duplicating a report in src/api/reports.ts (line 171), the code concatenates `${source.name} (copy)` and then calls `truncate(..., MAX_NAME_LENGTH)`. Because `MAX_NAME_LENGTH` is 120 and report names can already be up to 120 characters long, adding ` (copy)` exceeds the maximum length. Consequently, `truncate` cuts off the end and replaces the final characters with `...` (effectively replacing ` (copy)` or part of it with `...`), resulting in a name ending in `...` instead of `(copy)`. To fix this, the source name should be truncated first to leave enough room for ` (copy)`, or ` (copy)` should be appended after appropriately truncating the source name (e.g. truncating to `MAX_NAME_LENGTH - 7` characters before appending ` (copy)`).

args.title: Triage issue 4434
args.body:
File: src/components/UploadForm.tsx

In src/components/UploadForm.tsx, the file input's onChange handler sets `setFile(e.target.files?.[0] ?? null)` but does not clear any existing error state (`setProblem(null)`). When a new file is chosen after an upload error, the old error message and row number remain visible under the form until the user submits the form again. The fix is to add `setProblem(null)` inside the file input's onChange handler (or update the file state setter).
